title: Mining water ice in permanently shadowed craters
bottleneck: The richest lunar water deposits lie in craters that have not seen sunlight in billions of years — but we do not know the ice's form (pure slabs, grain coatings, or mixed with regolith), its depth distribution, or its concentration at any specific site. Excavation at -230 C in darkness, capturing volatiles without losing water to vacuum sublimation during handling, and doing it all robotically with no servicing are each unsolved. All current knowledge comes from orbital remote sensing; no one has touched PSR ice.
why_it_blocks: Lunar propellant and life support hinge on this ice; if it is patchy, deep, or low-grade, the business case for lunar ISRU changes completely.
current_state: Orbital data from LRO and LCROSS confirm hydrogen signatures; VIPER's cancellation removed the near-term ground-truth mission. No extraction demonstration exists.
